title: Intrinsic finite-Tor presentation of canonical refinement comparison
statement: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a quasi-compact morphism of schemes, and $c,d$ compactifications of $f$. Write $\mathcal C_{X,R}=D^b_{ctf}(X_{proet},R)$ for the intrinsic constant-ring module full subcategory [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and $F_c=Rp_*j_!$ for its ambient compact-support candidate [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. Let $V_T=E_{T,R}\nu_T^*$ be the ordinary etale inverse image followed by the fixed-module-to-intrinsic realization, with support presentation $a_c$ [def-sp-et-proet-coefficient-transport]. This definition gives the intrinsic finite-Tor presentation of the canonical etale-origin compactification comparison [def-pur-origin-compactification-comparison]. For a bounded-below etale complex $E$, let $s_c(E):F_c V_X(E)\simeq V_Y(F_{c,et}E)$ be $a_c$ followed by the specified proper-mate/open site comparison [def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction], and set $r_{c,d}(E)=s_c(E)\,V_Y(I^{et}_{c,d}(E))\,s_d(E)^{-1}$ in left-to-right order, where $I^{et}_{c,d}$ is the specified etale common-refinement comparison [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Say a natural isomorphism $\rho:\iota F_c\simeq\iota F_d$ is normalized when, for every $Q\in\mathcal C_{X,R}$, every bounded-below etale $E$, and every isomorphism $t:V_X(E)\simeq\iota Q$, its component is $\rho_Q=F_c(t^{-1})\,r_{c,d}(E)\,F_d(t)$. There exists exactly one normalized natural isomorphism: every intrinsic bounded constructible object has an etale origin and comparison is fully faithful [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Define the intrinsic finite-Tor refinement comparison to be this unique normalized natural isomorphism. Thus no arbitrary isomorphism or etale-origin restriction on the input is supplied.

source.place: Locality; Tags 0F7I and 0F7J (common-refinement comparison); Tag 099R (fully faithful bounded-below etale comparison).

proof.text: Restrict the exact fixed-module comparison to bounded-below etale complexes. The existing derived Hom bijection gives fullness there, and postcomposition with the intrinsic realization equivalence preserves fullness. Thus V = inclusion followed by site is full.

For an intrinsic Dctf input Q, its constructible cohomology and boundedness put it in the essential image of the finite-ring constructible derived comparison. Its bounded etale antecedent lies in D-plus. The derived functor composition isomorphism identifies that comparison with site, giving an antecedent for V.

Whisker and reassociate the support presentation and canonical compact-support site comparison to obtain natural supportSite isomorphisms on D-plus. Conjugate the specified etale common-refinement isomorphism by these. Its component is exactly refinementModel, by the component formulas for whiskering, associators and functorial images of isomorphisms.

Choose an etale antecedent E_Q and identification t_Q for each intrinsic input Q. Define its component as F_c(t_Q inverse), followed by the origin comparison at E_Q, followed by F_d(t_Q). To prove naturality, lift t_Q composed with any ambient arrow composed with t_Qprime inverse through the full functor V, apply origin naturality, and cancel the identification isomorphisms. To prove normalization for any other antecedent E and s, lift s composed with t_Q inverse and apply the same naturality and cancellation. The components are isomorphisms, so they define the desired natural isomorphism. Any normalized isomorphism agrees at each chosen E_Q,t_Q, hence equals this one by natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality. The definition refinement selects precisely the uniquely normalized isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: The existing declaration docstring descent argument, formalized using the existing finite-ring origin and derived Hom-bijection theorems. The generic categorical descent and normalization glue is proved privately in the item module; no new proof obligation is introduced.
